author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: Add an HTTP Ingest integration in Sophos Fusion, then call setPushEventSettings with serviceType jsonRPC, the integration URL, and authorization set to "Bearer <Integration Key>". Each POST is one record. Antimalware (av), HyperDetect (hd) and Exchange (exchange-malware) detections go to Antivirus; EDR and XDR incidents, Advanced Threat Control, Anti-Exploit, Network Attack Defense, ransomware mitigation, Sandbox Analyzer and Antiphishing go to the third-party alert schema. Incident workflow, health and management modules stay generic. A parser makes one event per record, so when Bitdefender batches several events in one POST only the first is normalized; events_in_batch records the batch size and the whole body stays in generic. Check the batch sizes you get before you rely on it. Only incidents carry a vendor severity; the others are set to MEDIUM, or HIGH for ransomware mitigation, Sandbox Analyzer and Anti-Exploit. The CEF and Splunk service types aren't covered: Bitdefender doesn't publish their fields. Samples follow Bitdefender's JSON-RPC message examples with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-13, and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. On 2026-10-14 each child also passed Run Test in a lab tenant as a separate parser under its parent. The engine also stored event_type (the module) on the antivirus records, a field its antivirus schema has but the docs' schema table doesn't list. No built-in parser in that tenant matched these records.
